 Game Preview: Warriors at Dallas Mavericks - 11/18/26
 Kalyb Champion Writer & Digital Content Coordinator November 17, 2026 11:20 AM PST WARRIORS AND MAVERICKS ATTEMPT TO SNAP LOSING STREAKS 
The Warriors head to Dallas to face Cooper Flagg, Kyrie Irving, and the Mavericks at American Airlines Arena on Wednesday. The Dubs and Mavericks both enter Tuesday’s game looking to snap a three-game losing streak. The Mavericks have won three straight home games though — their losing streak came on a road trip. 
 Wednesday's game is a highly-anticipated matchup for Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg as he faces his college coach Dusty May, his college teammate Morez Johnson Jr. and his favorite player Kyrie Irving. Lendeborg won a National Championship alongside May and Johnson at Michigan and is from New Jersey, Irving's childhood hometown. 
 Tap To Watch
 LAST TIME OUT 
The Warriors fell 115-94 against the New Orleans Pelicans at Smoothie King Center on Monday night, dropping their third consecutive game. The Pelicans held a wire-to-wire victory, scoring the first basket of the game and never trailing. Jeremiah Fears recorded his first career triple-double for the Pelicans, finishing the game with 19 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists. Saddiq Bey scored a team-high 23 points for the Pelicans and was one of six players to score in double figures. Yaxel Lendeborg scored a game-high 28 points, while Brandin Podziemski added 15 points. »Full Story

Injury Management) are questionable. Stephen Curry (Right Oblique Tear), Jimmy Butler III (Right ACL Repair / Surgery), Moses Moody (Left Patellar Tendon Repair / Surgery), Brandon Williams (Left Hamstring Strain) and Kristaps Porzingis (Not With Team) are OUT. Team Notes 
 DAL: Walter Clayton Jr. (Right Ankle Sprain) and Santi Aldama (Left Ankle Sprain) are probable. Max Christe (Left Ankle Sprain) is questionable. Dereck Lively II (Right Foot Surgery), Sergio de Larrea (Right Knee Sprain) and Tarik Biberovic (Right Heel Bursitis) are OUT. Team Notes

 COMPELLING NOTE: 
 Warriors:  The Warriors matched their longest losing streak of the season, dropping their third consecutive game on Tuesday. The Dubs are 1-3 without Stephen Curry this season and also lost when he got injured in the first quarter against the Houston Rockets on Nov. 11. 
 Mavericks:  In his first season back from a torn ACL, Kyrie Irving is one of four qualified players averaging at least 20 points (22.7 PPG) and shooting 39% or better from three (39.8 3PT%) on at least eight attempts per game (8.9 3PA). Irving joins Luka Doncic, Stephen Curry and Paul George.
